messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

Consydre is an imperative urging moral self-examination Consydre
thou makes the address direct thou
myne condicyon situates the speaker in distress myne
reflecte calls the speaker to deliberate reflection reflecte
fader names the vulnerable elder fader
Shall forms a rhetorical question rather than a request for information Shall
forsake is the central moral act being rejected forsake
strycken wyth blyndnesse describes the father’s disabling condition strycken
destytute indicates helplessness destytute
wrastle wyth infirmitie portrays the struggle against weakness wrastle
penurye adds economic need penurye
lyeth wythin my poure asserts that the speaker has the ability to help lyeth
rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye states the desirable outcome rendre
Archaisms signal a historical English register Archaisms
Rhetoric appeals to pity, duty, and conscience Rhetoric
